trust_decision.summary: The router decides whether downstream request payload may be written to a (possibly shared, keep-alive) upstream HTTP/1 connection before the upstream has accepted the upgrade; at the pinned commit it pauses only CONNECT and WebSocket upgrades, so generic-upgrade payload is sent raw (unchunked) and can be parsed by the backend as a pipelined request if the upgrade is rejected.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'generic (non-WebSocket) upgrade'; this is the only place that branches on isWebSocketUpgradeRequest to set a pause flag before newStream().

fix_sites.entry_point: Downstream HTTP/1 request with Connection: upgrade + non-websocket Upgrade, or HTTP/2/3 extended CONNECT with :protocol, routed by the HCM router to an HTTP/1 cluster (UpstreamRequest::acceptHeadersFromRouter)
UpstreamRequest::onPoolReady for non-HTTP generic upstreams (TCP/UDP CONNECT termination) — must clear the new flag
UpstreamCodecFilter::decodeHeaders (terminal upstream HTTP filter) — returns StopAllIterationAndWatermark to buffer body
UpstreamCodecFilter::CodecBridge::decodeHeaders (upstream response headers) — unpauses on 101, or 2xx on non-HTTP/1.1 upstream

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All source changes stay inside source/common/router plus the interface in envoy/http/filter.h:246-247 and a runtime guard; no second implementation or lower-level module is changed.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver could argue the HTTP/1 connection pool (source/common/http/http1/conn_pool.cc:58-76) is the right/only layer and that pausing the router is out of scope, or conversely that terminated CONNECT-UDP/TCP upstreams 'are not upgrades' and skip the onPoolReady unpause, deadlocking them.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Generic-upgrade payload must still flow: (a) for terminated CONNECT-UDP/TCP (non-HTTP generic upstream, protocol unset) the pause must be cleared at pool-ready or capsules sent before the synthesized 200 deadlock; (b) on HTTP/2/3 upstreams a 2xx accepts the upgrade; (c) on HTTP/1 a 101 releases buffered bytes; (d) headers-only upgrade requests (end_stream) must not be paused; (e) existing WebSocket timeout/4xx-5xx handling must stay intact. An over-broad fix (dropping all pre-accept payload, or pausing every upstream) breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: HTTP/1 downstream: Connection: upgrade + Upgrade: <non-websocket token> with body
HTTP/2 downstream extended CONNECT (:protocol) transformed to H1 upgrade (source/common/http/http2/codec_impl.cc:607-608)
Connection header with multiple tokens e.g. 'keep-alive, Upgrade' (source/common/http/utility.cc:668-674)
Upstream response 101 vs 2xx on H2/H3 upstream vs 200 on H1 upstream (rejected)
Non-HTTP generic upstream (TCP/UDP termination) where protocol is unset

O8b_injection_room.sibling: HTTP/1 pool returns the connection to the pool after an upgrade request whose upgrade was rejected and whose request side completed; a planted variant could also flag 'upgrade request' streams as reusable.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The pool decides reuse only from encode/decode completion and Connection: close (conn_pool.cc:50-51,63-68), never from upgrade state; a maintainer optimising keep-alive could plausibly not consider upgrades.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Pause decision reads parent_.downstreamHeaders() before upstream HTTP filters run, while the HTTP/1 codec decides raw (unchunked) framing on the headers it actually encodes (codec_impl.cc:472-479); a planted upstream filter/header mutation that adds Upgrade/Connection would create a check-vs-use differential.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Upstream HTTP filters and header mutation are designed to edit request headers after the router; the two isUpgrade calls are on different header snapshots in different layers.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: decodeTrailers/decodeMetadata only ASSERT on pausedForConnect; a planted path that forwards trailers or metadata while pausedForGenericUpgrade would leak bytes pre-acceptance.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Existing asserts cover only CONNECT; extending them to new pause kinds is easy to forget.

O9_family: HTTP request smuggling / response queue poisoning (CWE-444): front proxy treats bytes as opaque upgrade payload while the HTTP/1 backend parses them as a pipelined request after rejecting the upgrade.

O10_build.toolchain: Bazel (envoy build image / clang), very heavy first build
O10_build.project_tests: test/integration/websocket_integration_test.cc (NonWebsocketUpgrade), test/integration/udp_tunneling_integration_test.cc, test/common/router/upstream_codec_filter_test.cc, test/common/router/upstream_request_test.cc; integration tests use in-process fake upstreams

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Widen the WebSocket branch at upstream_request.cc:394 to all isUpgrade() requests, inheriting the WebSocket sendLocalReply-on-non-101 and timeout behaviour, or forget to clear the pause for non-HTTP (TCP/UDP-terminated) upstreams in onPoolReady.

out_of_scope_notes: tcp_proxy HTTP tunneling builds its own CONNECT/POST headers (source/common/tcp_proxy/upstream.cc:147-179) and is not a generic-upgrade route.
generic_proxy HTTP/1 codec rejects upgrade and CONNECT outright (source/extensions/filters/network/generic_proxy/codecs/http1/config.cc:101-107).
